findings.title: Public group member pages now silently omit members after the first 50
findings.body: The members action applies a default limit of 50 to every group, but the public group-members route/template has no pagination controls or actions that change offset. Consequently, visiting a visible group with more than 50 members only renders the first 50 and provides no way to see the rest. Previously non-automatic groups returned their full membership list.

findings.title: Pagination creates an extra empty page for exact multiples of the page size
findings.body: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When a group has exactly 50, 100, etc. members, this reports one more page than exists; for example, 50 members reports 2 pages and Next requests offset 50, which returns an empty member list. Use a ceiling calculation (while retaining the zero-member case) so the last-page guard is correct.

findings.title: Existing PATCH membership requests now make groups invisible
findings.body: The resource route still dispatches PATCH /admin/groups/:id to update, but this action no longer handles the former changes add/delete payload. A legacy PATCH request containing only changes therefore ignores the membership mutation and executes group.visible = (nil == "true"), setting visible to false while returning success. The previous implementation handled PATCH separately and preserved group attributes. Preserve the PATCH behavior or reject it explicitly rather than silently changing visibility.

findings.title: Out-of-order member-list responses can overwrite the selected page
findings.body: Each findMembers response unconditionally writes offset and members to the shared group model. The route now starts the initial request without waiting for it, and the Next/Previous actions can start another request while it is pending. If the older request finishes after the newer one, it restores the older page and offset, so an admin can click Next and end up viewing the first page again. Requests need sequencing/cancellation or the response must be ignored unless it matches the current requested offset.

findings.title: Automatic groups display unusable remove-member controls
findings.body: This template is rendered as an itemView for `member in members`, so its context is the member user. The unqualified `automatic` lookup therefore does not read the containing group and is normally undefined, making `unless automatic` true. Remove icons are shown for automatic groups even though the server rejects the delete request with 422. Pass/reference the parent group’s automatic flag in the item view instead.
